note: First calendar, made mid-week from the first research scans. Long-form days are listed but produced as Shorts until the long-form system exists. The full weekly calendar arrives Monday 16 Nov.

items.topic: The Pudding Guy: a man bought thousands of pudding cups to collect a mountain of airline miles
items.angle: Ordinary person beats a big company with its own promotion (loophole)
items.title: This Man Bought $3,000 of Pudding for Free Flights
items.why: Loophole / genius-trick Shorts are the strongest signal this week (e.g. 'The Craziest Supermarket Loophole', 4.7M views). The Pudding Guy itself broke out at ~100x on another channel.

items.topic: Pepsi's Harrier jet: a Pepsi Points ad showed a fighter jet as a prize and a student tried to collect it
items.angle: Brand's own ad backfires; ordinary person calls the bluff
items.title: Pepsi Accidentally Offered a Fighter Jet
items.why: Pepsi is the most frequent brand in this week's hit titles; brand + shock title pattern.

items.topic: Hoover's free-flights promotion: buy a vacuum, get two free flights — and it cost the company a fortune
items.angle: Promotion loophole; the company loses, the customers win
items.title: Hoover Gave Away Free Flights. It Cost Them Millions.
items.why: Same loophole signal; titles with money words are in ~38% of this week's hit Shorts.
items.long_later: Long version idea: People Who Beat Giant Companies at Their Own Game (Pudding Guy, Pepsi jet, Hoover)

items.topic: Blockbuster laughed at the chance to buy Netflix for $50 million
items.angle: Everyone laughed at it — then it became worth billions
items.title: Blockbuster Laughed at Netflix for $50 Million
items.why: 'Products everyone made fun of, later made billions' broke out at ~15x this week; 'rise and fall' is the top long-form pattern.
items.long_later: Long version idea: Whatever Happened to Blockbuster?
